Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: You get a frantic call from your friend whose car has broken down on the side of the highway late at night, and they need you to come get them immediately.
Situation2: An irate long-time customer challenges the legitimacy of the offer and demands thorough explanations.
Story: My phone buzzed with a frantic call from Sam, my oldest friend. “My car broke down on the highway. I’m scared. Can you come get me? Please?” I could hear the panic in his voice, and my heart twisted. Of course I wanted to help him—he’d do the same for me. But at that exact moment, I was on a call with Mrs. Jenkins, a long-time customer who was furious about the new offer I was pitching. “This sounds like a scam! Explain it again, and don’t leave anything out!” she snapped, her voice sharp in my headset. My manager always reminded us: never hang up on a customer, especially one as important as Mrs. Jenkins. I was expected to stay calm, answer every question, and keep her trust. But Sam was alone, scared, and counting on me. My hands shook as I tried to listen to Mrs. Jenkins’ tirade while staring at Sam’s desperate text messages. I felt torn in two, the weight of both expectations pressing down on me, and I didn’t know which role I could bear to let down.
